Zero-copy I/O core: memfile-backed inputs, reusable outputs.

Replaces streams throughout the library. Input is a read cursor over either a memory-mapped file (zero-copy, no read syscalls, no buffer copies) or an owned/shared string. Output is a reusable growable buffer: pass the same Output across calls and reset it to avoid repeated allocation. Span is a borrowed pointer+length view, valid only while its parent Input/Output lives.

Types

Input = ref object of RootObj
Read cursor. One of str (string-backed) or map (mmap-backed) keeps the memory alive; keep extends that to derived views (e.g. Output converted via toInput). 
IoError = object of CatchableError
MapHandle = ref object
  size*: int
Owns a read-only file mapping. Closed idempotently. 
Output = ref object of RootObj
  len*: int
Reusable write buffer. buf may over-allocate; len is used. 
Span = object
  p*: pointer
  len*: int
Borrowed view into Input/Output memory. Copy is a memcpy; the parent must outlive any use.
